title: The Yangtze still has a porpoise
description: China closed its longest river to fishing for ten years. The finless porpoise recovered. The Chinese sturgeon, endangered for another reason, did not.

title: What actually happens when a species goes extinct
description: On Guam the consequence was measured. When the baiji left the Yangtze, there was no baseline to measure against. The loss was the same size.

title: The lead ban worked and the poisonings rose
description: California banned lead ammunition twice, and condor lead deaths went up. An analysis of nearly three decades of records explains how both can be true.

title: Where money for endangered species actually goes
description: What charity ratings measure, what they leave out, and why the structure of a gift decides more than a star score does.

title: Engraving the rarest tortoise, and what it did not stop
description: Serial numbers are cut into ploughshare tortoise shells to ruin their black-market value. Within two years, marked animals were being sold anyway.

title: CITES governs borders, not habitat
description: The third list people confuse with the other two. What the treaty controls, what it cannot touch, and why a party can opt out of any listing it dislikes.

title: The people who vaccinate Ethiopia's wolves
description: In 2019 rabies and distemper reached the Bale Mountains together and the outbreak ran past 220 days. What that changed about how the wolves are vaccinated.

title: The axolotl is not extinct in the wild
description: Extinct in the Wild is a category with a written test, and the axolotl does not meet it. What the Xochimilco counts counted, and what 2025 found.

title: What the IUCN Red List is, and what it is not
description: An assessment of extinction risk, made by named groups under a published standard. It is not a law, and it does not decide what gets protected.

title: How much of the Earth is actually protected
description: About a sixth of the land and a twelfth of the sea, by the latest global count. What the figures include, why they move, and how far they are from thirty.

title: What the endangered species apps actually do
description: No app tracks which species are at risk. The stores offer identification tools, a showcase last updated in 2021, and fundraising products.

title: The crane that had to be taught where to go
description: Whooping cranes learn their migration route by flying it with older birds. What that means for a species rebuilt from captivity, and what it puts at risk.

title: What critically endangered actually means
description: The highest threatened category on the IUCN Red List, the five criteria an assessor applies, and why the label describes risk rather than rarity.

title: The Iberian lynx and the arithmetic of coming back
description: The 2025 census counted 2,663 Iberian lynx and then said the number is a floor, not an estimate. Why success makes a population harder to count.

title: How many vaquita are left
description: The most recent survey saw between seven and ten, and at least one calf. What that number counts, and why published figures disagree.
